title: Pruning is shipped OFF: the retention value is a product decision, so ISS-JOBQLOST-001 is only closed once the wiring unit sets pruneTerminalAfterMs
evidence: Pruning forgets the job id: after it, enqueue of the same id returns 'enqueued' (a NEW job) instead of 'exists', and a late complete/fail of a pruned job answers not-found instead of terminal. The retention therefore is the idempotency window for producers that retry enqueue. Pinned by file-job-queue.prune.test.ts.
fix_direction: The wiring unit must choose the value (longer than the longest producer retry horizon and any late-ack window) and pass it; Umesh decision.

title: Pruning runs only inside a successful operation that names a tenant: an idle tenant keeps its terminal jobs, a tenant-less claim prunes nothing, and every operation still rewrites the whole (live) file
evidence: Tenant scope was chosen so one tenant operations never delete another tenant history. Consequence pinned by test 'tenant scope': claim(worker) with no tenant prunes nothing. Lock hold time still grows with the number of non-terminal jobs.
fix_direction: If a tenant-less maintenance sweep is wanted, add an explicit prune(tenantId) call from a janitor; not needed while every wired caller passes tenantId.

title: Other lock-eperm wall-clock-budget cases still use small lockWaitMs values (80 ms, never-clears case 300 ms) that only need to be exceeded, not met
evidence: Only the clearing case needed a large budget and was raised to 5000 ms; the never-clears and past-budget cases assert conflict, which a coarser tick can only make more certain. Original file ran 19/20 on this machine under light load (5/20-8/20 failing under load per ISS-JOBQPID-003), fixed file 30/30.
fix_direction: None needed; noted so a later reader does not tighten them back.
